drugs.notes:
IV artesunate for severe malaria. Give IV (preferred) or IM. Always follow with full 3-day oral ACT (Coartem) once patient can tolerate oral. Monitor Hb weekly for 4 weeks for post-artesunate delayed hemolysis (PADH).

Weight-based dosing:
• <20kg: 3.0 mg/kg per dose
• ≥20kg: 2.4 mg/kg per dose

Vials needed per dose:
• ≤25kg: 1 vial
• 26-50kg: 2 vials
• 51-75kg: 3 vials
• 76-100kg: 4 vials
drugs.referral_trigger_text: Below 5kg or under 2 months old: refer immediately for specialist care.
drugs.iv_info:
[conc:20]Reconstitute:
1. Add 3ml of provided arginine/NaHCO₃ solvent to 60mg artesunate vial
2. Shake gently until clear (~1 min)
3. Final concentration = 20mg/ml → draw [ml]ml
• ≤25kg child: use 1 vial per dose (round up to 2ml minimum)

Give slow IV over 1-2 min (do NOT further dilute for IV push).
Use within 1 hour of reconstitution.
Discard if solution is not clear.

Always follow with full 3-day oral ACT (Coartem) once patient can swallow.
Monitor Hb weekly for 4 weeks for post-artesunate delayed hemolysis (PADH).
drugs.safety_warning: Monitor for post-artesunate delayed hemolysis (PADH) — check Hb weekly for 4 weeks after treatment.
drugs.source_name: WHO Severe Malaria Guidelines + MMV Injectable Artesunate Toolkit (WHO PQ MA168)
drugs.source_detail: WHO: 3mg/kg <20kg, 2.4mg/kg ≥20kg at 0, 12, 24h. Reconstitute with 3ml solvent = 20mg/ml. CDC confirms same regimen.

drugs.notes:

drugs.notes:
Low-dose radical cure for P. vivax: 0.25mg/kg/day × 14 days. Practical weight-band table derived from 7.5mg and 15mg tablet strengths.

IMPORTANT: Distinguish two uses of primaquine:
  1) Radical cure (P. vivax): 0.25mg/kg/day × 14 days — G6PD testing required
  2) Transmission-blocking single dose (P. falciparum): 0.25mg/kg single dose — safe without G6PD testing

If G6PD deficient: use 0.75mg/kg once weekly × 8 weeks instead of daily dosing.

Very few children under 8kg qualify for primaquine radical cure at health centre level (referral only).

G6PD testing recommended before treatment per Ethiopia national guidelines.

Reconstitute:

• 500mg vial + 4.8ml sterile water = 100mg/ml → draw [ml]ml

Infuse over 30 min (60 min in neonates).
Do NOT use calcium-containing fluids (Ringer's, Hartmann's).

drugs.notes:
Dosed on the amoxicillin component. Standard dose: 25mg/kg/dose of amoxicillin component twice daily for mild-moderate infections. High dose: 45mg/kg/dose for severe/resistant cases. Syrup ratios are always expressed as amoxicillin/clavulanate.

Commonly available syrups:
- 125mg/31.25mg per 5ml (4:1 ratio)
- 200mg/28.5mg per 5ml (7:1 ratio)
- 250mg/62.5mg per 5ml (4:1 ratio)
- 400mg/57mg per 5ml (7:1 ratio)

Tablets: 375mg, 625mg (500/125), 1g (875/125)
drugs.safety_warning: Weight-based: 25mg/kg/dose of amoxicillin component BID for standard dose, up to 45mg/kg/dose BID for high dose (severe infections, treatment failure, or areas with high penicillin resistance). Clarithromycin ratio varies — always verify the specific product available.

drugs.source_detail: 25-45 mg/kg/dose of amoxicillin component twice daily. Mild-moderate: lowest effective dose. Severe: high dose (45 mg/kg/dose, up to 1.5g per dose).

drugs.drug_name_en: RL (Ringer's Lactate IV — Plan C, severe dehydration)
drugs.dose_display_en:
WHO PLAN C — Severe Dehydration

Total: 100 ml/kg IV Ringer's Lactate (= [CALC: weight × 100] ml total)

If age <12 months:
  Step 1: 30 ml/kg IV over 1 hour (= [CALC: weight × 30] ml)
  Step 2: 70 ml/kg IV over 5 hours (= [CALC: weight × 70] ml)

If age ≥12 months:
  Step 1: 30 ml/kg IV over 30 minutes (= [CALC: weight × 30] ml)
  Step 2: 70 ml/kg IV over 2.5 hours (= [CALC: weight × 70] ml)

Example (10kg child ≥12mo):
  30 × 10 = 300ml over 30 min, then 70 × 10 = 700ml over 2.5h
  Total = 1000ml

Reassess every 15-30 minutes.
Give ORS 5ml/kg/hour once child can drink.
Give Zinc 20mg/day (10mg if <6mo) for 14 days.
drugs.notes: WHO Plan C for severe dehydration with diarrhea. Use Ringer's Lactate first line. Normal Saline if RL unavailable. For severe acute malnutrition (SAM), use ReSoMal or half-strength standard ORS with added K+ and glucose — do NOT use standard Plan C volumes.
drugs.safety_warning: Reassess the child every 15-30 minutes during IV therapy. If child has severe acute malnutrition (SAM), do NOT use standard Plan C — use ReSoMal or special SAM protocol instead.
drugs.source_name: WHO IMCI Guidelines — Plan C for Severe Dehydration
drugs.source_detail: 100ml/kg total. Age-dependent timing: <12mo: 30ml/kg/1hr + 70ml/kg/5hrs. ≥12mo: 30ml/kg/30min + 70ml/kg/2.5hrs.

drugs.notes: For bacterial gastroenteritis (Salmonella, Shigella) not responding to oral antibiotics. 150mg/kg/day divided q8h. HIDDEN — only shown when severe/professional use needed.
drugs.safety_warning: Adjust dose in renal impairment. Monitor for C. difficile diarrhea.
drugs.source_name: WHO pediatric ceftazidime dosing guidelines
drugs.source_detail: 150mg/kg/day IV divided q8h for bacterial gastroenteritis. Good gram-negative coverage including Pseudomonas.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Zinc 20mg once daily for 14 days
(Give 10mg once daily if child is under 6 months of age)

WHO recommendation: 20mg/day (10mg/day for infants <6mo) for 14 days, regardless of weight. Reduces diarrhea duration and prevents future episodes.
drugs.referral_trigger_text: Under 2 months: zinc not recommended. Refer for diarrhea management.
drugs.safety_warning: Zinc may cause mild gastric irritation — give with food. Persistent vomiting may require dose adjustment.
drugs.source_name: WHO/UNICEF diarrhea management guideline (2024 update)
drugs.source_detail: Zinc 20mg/day (10mg if <6 months) for 14 days for all children with acute diarrhea. Not weight-dependent.

drugs.dose_display_en:
ORS — Plan A (No Dehydration): Give ORS as tolerated after each loose stool.
• <2 years: 50-100ml after each stool
• ≥2 years: 100-200ml after each stool

ORS — Plan B (Some Dehydration): Give ORS based on weight over 4 hours.
• 75ml/kg over 4 hours
Example (10kg child): 10 × 75ml = 750ml total

ORS — Plan C (Severe Dehydration): Refer to IV Plan C (RL).

Also give Zinc 20mg/day (10mg if <6 months) for 14 days.
Continue breastfeeding/feeding.
drugs.notes: ORS is the mainstay of diarrhea management. Assess dehydration status before deciding Plan A, B, or C. Weight is essential for Plan B calculation — always enter both weight and age.
drugs.referral_trigger_text: Unable to drink or keep down ORS, signs of severe dehydration, or blood in stool (possible dysentery): refer to higher level.
drugs.safety_warning: If child vomits ORS, wait 10 minutes then try again more slowly (spoon or dropper, 1-2ml every 2-3 minutes). If persistent vomiting, consider IV fluids. Monitor for stool output to adjust ORS intake mL-for-mL for ongoing losses.
drugs.source_name: WHO IMCI / UNICEF Diarrhea Treatment Guidelines
drugs.source_detail: ORS is the core treatment for diarrhea. Plan A (home), Plan B (facility, 75ml/kg over 4h), Plan C (IV, severe dehydration). Weight and age both required.

drugs.notes:
Acute asthma management:

INHALER PUFFS (via spacer) — age-based — preferred route:
  <2 years: 2-4 puffs q20min × 1hr (via spacer with mask), then 2-4 puffs q4h PRN
  2-5 years: 4-6 puffs q20min × 1hr, then 4 puffs q4h PRN
  >5 years: 6-8 puffs q20min × 1hr, then 6-8 puffs q4h PRN

NEBULIZED (Salbutamol 5mg/ml respiratory solution):
  <5 years: 2.5mg (0.5ml) q20min × 1hr, then q4h
  ≥5 years: 5mg (1ml) q20min × 1hr, then q4h

SYRUP (if no inhaler/spacer available):
  <2 years: 0.1-0.15mg/kg/dose TID-QID (syrup: 2mg/5ml)
  2-5 years: 1-2mg TID-QID
  >5 years: 2-4mg TID-QID

drugs.referral_trigger_text: ACUTE SEVERE ASTHMA: unable to speak, severe chest indrawing, cyanosis, silent chest, exhaustion. Give first dose (inhaled salbutamol + prednisolone) and REFER URGENTLY. This is a medical emergency.
drugs.safety_warning: Inhaled via spacer is preferred over nebulized (equally effective, less side effects). Salbutamol may cause tachycardia, tremor, hypokalemia with high doses. Monitor for signs of severe exacerbation — silent chest is a life-threatening sign.
drugs.source_name: GINA 2024 / BTS/SIGN 2023 / WHO IMCI acute asthma
drugs.source_detail: Age-based inhaler puff dosing via spacer. First-line acute bronchodilator. Inhaled route preferred over oral. Nebulized as alternative.

Hydrocortisone IV (age-based dosing):

If age <1 year:
  25mg IV every 6 hours

If age 1-5 years:
  50mg IV every 6 hours

If age 6-12 years:
  100mg IV every 6 hours

OR weight-based: 4mg/kg/dose IV q6h (max 100mg/dose)

Give by slow IV injection over at least 1 minute.
Continue until patient stabilizes, typically 24-48 hours.
drugs.notes: For acute severe asthma / status asthmaticus when oral steroids cannot be given (vomiting, severe distress). For mild-moderate exacerbations, oral dexamethasone (0.6mg/kg single dose) is preferred. No taper needed for courses <7 days.
drugs.safety_warning: Monitor for hypernatremia if therapy extends beyond 48 hours. No advantage exists for higher corticosteroid doses in severe asthma exacerbations.
drugs.source_name: WHO/BTS GINA guidelines for acute asthma
drugs.source_detail: Age-based dosing per UK NHS guidelines. 4mg/kg/dose IV q6h alternative from BTS/SIGN.

drugs.dose_display_en:

0.6 mg/kg oral/IM single dose (max 16mg)

Weight-based quick reference:
  7-10 kg → 6mg
  11-20 kg → 10mg
  >20 kg → 16mg

Single dose is sufficient — equivalent to 5 days of prednisolone.
No discharge prescription needed for mild-moderate cases.

For PICU (critical asthma):

drugs.notes: Preferred over prednisolone for acute asthma exacerbations. Advantages: single dose, less vomiting, better compliance, longer half-life (36-54h). Use oral route if patient can swallow. Use IM if vomiting or severe distress. For PICU, use IV route.
drugs.referral_trigger_text: Not studied in children under 2 years. Evidence limited below this age.
drugs.safety_warning: Slightly higher ED return visits reported vs prednisolone (OR 1.07) but lower hospitalization rates (OR 0.90). Monitor for vomiting and mood changes.
drugs.source_name: Multiple RCTs + AAP/ACEP guidelines
drugs.source_detail: 0.6mg/kg single dose non-inferior to 5-day prednisolone. Standardized weight-band dosing validated in multiple pediatric ED studies.

drugs.notes: Range 1-2mg/kg/day. For acute moderate-severe asthma exacerbations. Single morning dose preferred (less HPA suppression). No taper needed for courses ≤7 days. Max 60mg/day.

drugs.source_name: WHO / CDC — chickenpox management
drugs.source_detail: Supportive care: calamine for itching, paracetamol for fever. Disease is self-limiting in immunocompetent children.

drugs.frequency_en: every 4-6 hours as needed for fever
drugs.safety_warning: Do NOT use ibuprofen in chickenpox (increased risk of secondary bacterial skin infections). Paracetamol only for fever.
drugs.source_name: WHO / standard pediatric fever reference
drugs.source_detail: 15mg/kg/dose q4-6h PRN fever. Max 60mg/kg/day. Ibuprofen NOT recommended in varicella.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Permethrin 5% cream — single application, repeat in 7 days

Apply to entire body FROM NECK DOWN (adults/older children).
For infants and children ≤2 years: apply to ENTIRE body including scalp, face, forehead, temples, and neck.

Leave on for 8-14 hours (overnight), then wash off.

Repeat once after 7 days.

TREAT ALL HOUSEHOLD CONTACTS simultaneously.
Wash bedding and clothing in hot water.

Itch may persist 4-6 weeks after successful treatment (post-scabies itch) — manage with emollients and antihistamines.
drugs.notes: First-line for scabies. Safe in children ≥2 months, pregnant and lactating women. Treat all household contacts even if asymptomatic. Oral ivermectin 200μg/kg single dose (repeat in 2 weeks) is alternative for children ≥15kg.
drugs.safety_warning: Skin irritation common — do NOT re-apply for irritation alone. Distinguish treatment irritation vs active scabies. Itch persisting >6 weeks suggests re-infestation.
drugs.source_name: WHO scabies guidelines / CDC / MSD Manual
drugs.source_detail: WHO: 5% permethrin first-line. Apply overnight, repeat day 7. Treat contacts. Oral ivermectin 200μg/kg is alternative.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Hydrocortisone 1% cream — apply to affected areas TWICE DAILY for 7-14 days

Use mild potency (hydrocortisone 1%) for face, neck, and flexures.
For body/trunk: use 1% cream BID.

Apply thin layer — do NOT overuse.
Limit continuous use on face to 7 days without review.

Taper: reduce frequency as eczema improves (e.g., switch to once daily for 3 days then stop).

No taper needed for courses <7 days.

For severe flares: consider moderate potency (betamethasone valerate 0.1%) for up to 14 days.
drugs.notes: Emollients (moisturizers) are the MAIN treatment for eczema — prescribe 250-500g weekly. Topical steroids are for FLARES only. Apply steroids FIRST, wait 15-30 min, then apply emollient.
drugs.safety_warning: Use lowest potency for shortest duration. On face: mild potency only (hydrocortisone 1%). Avoid prolonged use on face (risk of skin thinning, perioral dermatitis).
drugs.source_name: NICE guidelines / AAP / WHO EML
drugs.source_detail: Lowest potency (class VII) for children. 1% BID × 7-14 days for flares. Emollients are cornerstone of daily management.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Apply emollient LIBERALLY AND FREQUENTLY — at least 2-3 times daily, every day

Even when skin appears clear, continue daily use.

Apply AFTER bathing (pat skin dry, apply immediately).

Use as soap substitute (emollient wash) in bath/shower.

Weekly quantity:
  Infants: 250g/week
  Children: 500g/week

Choose: ointments (greasy but very effective), creams (less greasy), or lotions (light, for face).

Apply in direction of hair growth to prevent folliculitis.
drugs.notes: Cornerstone of eczema management. Emollients alone can control mild eczema. Use even when skin appears normal. No steroid should be prescribed without also prescribing an emollient.
drugs.safety_warning: Aqueous cream should NOT be used as leave-on moisturizer (causes skin irritation). Use as wash-off soap substitute only. Warn about flammability of paraffin-based emollients.
drugs.source_name: NICE CG57 / AAP atopic dermatitis guidelines
drugs.source_detail: Emollients are the foundation of eczema management. Prescribe 250-500g weekly. Apply liberally, frequently, continuously.

drugs.dose_display_en:
Clotrimazole 1% cream — apply TWICE DAILY for 2-4 weeks

Tinea corporis (body): BID × 2-4 weeks
Tinea cruris (groin): BID × 2 weeks
Tinea pedis (foot): BID × 4 weeks

Apply to affected area and 2cm beyond the border of the rash.

Continue for at least 1 week after symptoms resolve.

For scalp (tinea capitis), topical therapy alone is INSUFFICIENT — requires ORAL griseofulvin.
drugs.notes: First-line topical for localized dermatophyte infections. For extensive, scalp, or nail involvement, switch to oral therapy. Alternative to clotrimazole: terbinafine 1% cream once daily × 1 week (shorter course).
drugs.safety_warning: For tinea capitis (scalp ringworm), topical therapy alone is INSUFFICIENT — requires oral griseofulvin. Avoid combination steroid-antifungal creams (tinea incognito risk).
drugs.source_name: WHO EMLc / AAD guidelines / standard pediatric reference
drugs.source_detail: First-line topical: clotrimazole 1% BID × 2-4 weeks or terbinafine 1% once daily × 1 week. Oral therapy needed for scalp or extensive disease.

drugs.notes: For tinea capitis (scalp ringworm) or extensive tinea not responding to topical therapy. Administer with fatty meal (milk, peanut butter) to increase absorption. Terbinafine is alternative for Trichophyton species.
drugs.safety_warning: Contraindicated in liver failure, porphyria, pregnancy. Causes photosensitivity — avoid sun. Reduces OCP efficacy. Take with fatty meal.
drugs.source_name: WHO EMLc / AAP / Perth Children's Hospital ChAMP monograph
drugs.source_detail: Microsize: 20-25mg/kg/day PO once daily. Tinea capitis: 6-12 weeks. Tinea corporis: 2-4 weeks. Preferable for Microsporum species.

drugs.safety_warning: Take on empty stomach (1h before or 2h after meals). Monitor for rash, diarrhea.
drugs.source_name: WHO EMLc / standard pediatric reference
drugs.source_detail: 25-50mg/kg/day divided QID. Duration 5-7 days for uncomplicated cellulitis. Use higher end of range for severe cases.

drugs.safety_warning: Cloxacillin preferred if Staph suspected (most common cause of cellulitis). Amoxicillin covers Strep only.
drugs.source_name: Standard pediatric reference
drugs.source_detail: 40mg/kg/dose PO TID. Second-line for cellulitis. Cloxacillin preferred for antistaphylococcal coverage.

drugs.notes: Use for euvolemic children who cannot take adequate enteral fluids. For resuscitation/dehydration, use bolus therapy first (20 mL/kg NS/LR). Maintenance only AFTER resuscitation.
drugs.safety_warning: Monitor for fluid overload (edema, crackles, raised JVP). Check electrolytes within 24h. Do NOT use hypotonic fluids — risk of hyponatremia (AAP 2018). Two-thirds maintenance for unwell children with SIADH risk.
drugs.source_name: AAP 2018 / NICE NG29 / Holliday-Segar 1957
drugs.source_detail: 4-2-1 rule for maintenance (first 10kg: 4ml/kg/hr, 11-20kg: +2ml/kg/hr, >20kg: +1ml/kg/hr). Use isotonic fluids per AAP 2018 recommendation.

drugs.notes: Use isotonic crystalloids (NS or LR) only. Hypotonic fluids have NO role in resuscitation.
drugs.safety_warning: Reassess after EVERY bolus. If >40 mL/kg given without improvement, consider blood, inotropes, or referral. Do NOT give dextrose-containing fluids as rapid bolus (risk of hyperglycemia).
drugs.source_name: WHO IMCI / AAP PALS / NICE guidelines
drugs.source_detail: 20 mL/kg isotonic crystalloid bolus. Repeat as needed. Max 60 mL/kg before considering other interventions.

drugs.notes: Deficit replacement plus maintenance. NOT for immediate resuscitation (use bolus first). Always reassess hydration status regularly.
drugs.safety_warning: Replace deficit SLOWLY — rapid correction risks fluid overload. In hypernatremic dehydration, correct more slowly (over 48h). Monitor electrolytes, urine output, weight daily.
drugs.source_name: WHO IMCI / AAP / NICE NG29
drugs.source_detail: Deficit + maintenance over 24h: 50% in first 8h, 50% over next 16h. Deficit = weight(kg) × %dehydration × 10.

drugs.notes: For burns ≥15% TBSA in children (≥10% in young children). Parkland formula: 4 ml/kg/%TBSA. Calculate %TBSA using Lund-Browder chart or Wallace Rule of Nines (adjusted for children).
drugs.frequency_en: IV infusion over 24 hours (50% in 8h, 50% in 16h)
drugs.safety_warning: Monitor urine output (target 1-2 ml/kg/hr). Watch for fluid overload. Burn patients require particularly careful fluid management. Always consult a burn protocol for severe burns.
drugs.source_name: WHO Emergency Triage Assessment and Treatment / ATLS / Parkland formula
drugs.source_detail: Parkland: 4 ml/kg/%TBSA in 24h. Half in first 8h, half in next 16h. Common choice: Ringer's Lactate.
